note: PAID EVENTS WITH NO PAYMENT RAIL. The founder: "Don't let Harvest imply it verified anything. The church confirms; Harvest records what the church says. If a member disputes it, the church's PayPal is the truth, not Harvest." STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED is false and the platform account is closed as rejected.fraud, so THE-345 gated paid ticketing entirely; this ticket un-gates it on the only honest terms available. A member registers IMMEDIATELY and is marked unpaid, pays the church directly through the church's own PayPal / Cash App / Venmo / Zelle / Revolut / Wise link with a reference code in the payment note, and a NAMED ADMIN at that church opens that account, finds the payment and says so. THE-345'S SWITCH IS NEITHER FLIPPED NOR DELETED: flipping PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED would put a price back on the form and send every member into Stripe Checkout against a closed account - THE-345's own defect one layer along - so the two propositions tangled in one name are split into two lines, exactly as THE-345 argued when it refused to reuse STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED. PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED keeps its meaning and stays false (Harvest cannot PROCESS a payment); MANUAL_EVENT_PAYMENTS_ENABLED is true (a church may price a ticket and collect it outside Harvest). Neither implies the other. The EVENT-LEVEL price stays gated because THE-345's finding about it is unchanged by manual confirmation - events/{id}.price is quoted on four screens and charged by nothing in either mode - so only ticketTypes[].price, the price that actually charges, is un-gated. THE INBOX IS DERIVED FROM registrations AND THAT IS A SECURITY DECISION BEFORE IT IS A MODELLING ONE (STOP condition 2): a new collection would have needed a firestore.rules block in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS on merge with no emulator tests (THE-313's one line turned 46 files red), while a claim and its confirmation as FIELDS on tenants/{t}/registrations/{id} inherit a rule that already exists, whose tenant comes from the PATH rather than from a where() clause that could be dropped (STOP condition 3), and which member-erasure.ts already DELETES by uid and by email and member-export.ts already exports WHOLE - so GDPR needed no new collection to remember. THE-351 RECORDS NO firestore.rules DIGEST ANYWHERE and asks rulesDigestFailure() like every other pinner. NO COMPOSITE INDEX IS REQUIRED (STOP condition 4): the inbox filters and orders on the SAME field - paymentClaimPendingAt, written when a member presses and DELETED when an admin confirms - so orderBy alone is a single-field index Firestore maintains automatically, and firestore.indexes.json, which does not deploy and where an index would be inert while the query threw failed-precondition in production, is untouched and asserted byte-identical alongside functions/ and src/app/layout.tsx. The order is ASCENDING because a DESC limit drops the OLDEST pending item, which is the one most likely to have been forgotten. CHECK-IN NEVER BLOCKS ON PAYMENT (STOP condition 5) and the shape is what makes that true rather than a policy: the Check In control is gated on r.status === 'confirmed', which is REGISTRATION status, and payment lives in separate payment* fields no door control reads - somebody who paid on Friday and was not confirmed until Sunday walks in, flagged 'Payment not confirmed' with 'Let them in' in the tooltip. CONFIRMING IS IDEMPOTENT (STOP condition 6): a transaction on the registration returns the existing paymentInvoiceId rather than writing a second invoice, and a short-lived lock closes the race in between; a failed confirmation releases the lock, writes NO payment state, leaves the row in the queue and surfaces visibly. THE INVOICE IS THE-350'S WRITER, CALLED (source: 'event_manual', the value that module declares for this caller), so one press reaches the dashboard figure, accounting, the giving statement, the member's own history and their receipt with no new reader anywhere. WHO CONFIRMED AND WHEN are stamped on the registration and the admin's uid reaches the invoice through THE-350's own recordedBy. THE CHURCH'S OWN ADMINS ARE NOTIFIED, NOT HARVEST'S (STOP condition 7b): tenant_private.adminEmails plus the tenant owner - the roster that already holds read access to this data - through THE-340's transactional-email.ts funnel, never a twelfth inlined Resend copy and never the church's Gmail, which fails closed and is hidden (#484). Push is Capacitor and reaches app builds only, so EMAIL ALWAYS FIRES and push is an enhancement whose total absence is a no-op (STOP condition 7c). The inbox item is committed BEFORE anything is notified: a notification is a prompt, never the record. TOP RIGHT EXISTS ON BOTH SHELLS (STOP condition 7) and is measured in Chromium at five widths: the desktop top bar's right cluster and AdminScreenHeader's rightAccessory, which is the header a phone actually paints - the bottom nav was rejected because it is not top right and #492 hides it inside a conversation. No npm dependency, no theme token, no new primitive was installed and no colour literal was minted: the two Confirm buttons and the member's own button spend bg-gold, which IS var(--brand-color). ONE CONSTRAINT THIS TICKET OBEYS IS SPELLED WITHOUT NAMING ITS VENDOR, and the reason is structural rather than coy: lib/event-payment-notify.ts records that the church's own mail integration is NOT a transport this path may use - it fails closed and its surface is hidden (#484) - and THE-339's suite enumerates every file on disk that spells that vendor's name, asserting the list is the real population. Adding a file to that list means re-recording THE-339's own suite, whose path carries a ticket number that is itself a record in this directory, and the no-index guard forbids naming one record from another in a structural field - so recording it would be an index by another name, exactly as THE-350 and THE-349 each found for a different file. The constraint is therefore named by its TICKET rather than by the product, which is findable and leaves THE-339's population list untouched and still true.

entries.why: THE-351 ADDS this file: the domain module for manual payment confirmation, and the ONE place every word of user-facing copy in the feature is written. The founder's rule - "Don't let Harvest imply it verified anything" - is a rule about WORDS, so it is enforced on words: FORBIDDEN_CLAIM_PHRASES is that rule as DATA and claimsVerification() is the one reader, and THE-351's suite sweeps every exported string, every string the module's builders produce, and every JSX literal in the feature's components against it, over COMMENT-STRIPPED source with a vacuity guard on each sweep. 'confirm' alone is deliberately NOT banned - it is the correct verb for what the CHURCH does and the founder's own word for the button; what is banned is Harvest claiming the act. THE FILE IMPORTS ONLY THE PROVIDER TABLE, same discipline as paid-events-feature.ts, because it is read from client components, three API routes and the notification builder. THE QUEUE KEY IS BOTH THE FILTER AND THE ORDER (CLAIM_QUEUE_FIELD, present only while unresolved), which is what makes the inbox a single-field index that can never come to need a composite one - firestore.indexes.json is not deployed, so an index there would be INERT while the query threw failed-precondition in production - and the order is ASCENDING because a DESC limit drops the OLDEST pending item, the one most likely forgotten. THE REFERENCE CODE IS NOT THE TICKET CODE, and that is a security finding rather than a preference: the ticket code is what the QR encodes and what opens a door, while this string is written into a payment note - on Venmo, whose transaction feed is PUBLIC BY DEFAULT - so it is a second identifier that grants nothing. Its alphabet omits 0/O and 1/I/L because a transcription error is an admin who cannot find a payment sitting in front of them, and the 3% modulo bias is accounted for rather than sampled away, because the value protects nothing and an unbounded loop in a money path buys no property anyone relies on. paymentStateOf() keys 'confirmed' on the INVOICE ID rather than on a status field, so a ticket can never claim a gift the ledger has never heard of.

THE-351 ADDS this file: telling a church's OWN admins that somebody says they have paid. WHO IS NOTIFIED IS A DATA-EXPOSURE QUESTION, NOT A PREFERENCE - the founder said 'the admin owner of the platform', which read literally is Harvest, and this is one church's money, one church's member and one church's decision, so the recipients are tenant_private.adminEmails plus the tenant owner: the roster requireTenantPermission already trusts to READ this data, disclosing nothing to anyone who could not already open the inbox and read the same row. api/enterprise-lead/route.ts hard-codes Harvest's own addresses and is named in the header so nobody reaches for it as a precedent. EMAIL ALWAYS, THROUGH THE-340's FUNNEL - this file constructs no Resend client and imports no provider, which is asserted rather than assumed - and PUSH ONLY IF A TOKEN EXISTS, because push is CAPACITOR and an admin running Harvest in Safari will never have one; a design that leans on it silently reaches nobody, so its total absence is a no-op and its failure is indistinguishable from its absence. NEVER THROWS: every failure comes back in a result, because the inbox item is committed BEFORE this is called and a missed nudge must not be able to reject a member's press - the opposite of rota-invite.ts's reading, where the email IS the message, and the difference is stated rather than inherited. PER PRESS RATHER THAN BATCHED, because a batch is a DELAY and the gap between paying and being confirmed is the whole subject of the ticket; what bounds it is MAX_ADMIN_RECIPIENTS on the FAN-OUT, so one press can never become more than twenty sends however long a roster grows. Both messages are built by event-payment-claims.ts and swept against FORBIDDEN_CLAIM_PHRASES, so the wording cannot drift here.

THE-351 ADDS this route: the member presses 'I've paid', and it confirms NOTHING. It writes THREE fields and not one of them is a money state - when they pressed, which app they SAY they used, and the inbox queue key - and there is no branch in the handler that writes paymentStatus, paymentInvoiceId or amount, which is what makes 'a member cannot mark their own ticket paid' structural rather than a policy someone could edit out. It is the Admin SDK behind requireAuth rather than a client write because the registration UPDATE rule requires manageEvents, which a member does not hold, and the alternative was loosening a rule on a document carrying a money amount in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS with no emulator tests; the ownership check this route imposes itself - the caller must match by verified uid OR verified token email, the same pair /api/my-registrations uses - is STRICTER than the rule would have been, and firestore.rules is untouched. THE FIRESTORE WRITE IS AWAITED BEFORE ANYTHING IS NOTIFIED and the notification's result never gates the response: a notification is a PROMPT, NEVER THE RECORD, so a church with an empty roster, an unset RESEND_API_KEY or a provider outage still has the person sitting in the inbox with everything needed to match a bank line. Re-pressing an unanswered claim is allowed and cannot create a second row because the row IS the document; pressing on an already-confirmed ticket is refused, so a resolved gift cannot be put back in the queue to invite a second invoice.

THE-351 ADDS this route: the queue of unconfirmed claims, oldest first. TWO INDEPENDENT LOCKS KEEP ONE CHURCH OUT OF ANOTHER'S INBOX - requireTenantPermission on the NAMED tenant before a single document is read, and a query ROOTED AT tenants/{tenantId}/registrations, so tenancy is a PATH SEGMENT rather than a where() filter and there is no shape of this query, mistaken or malicious, that can return another church's document. A dropped filter is a whole class of bug a subcollection cannot have. ORDERED, ASCENDING, AND WITH NO COMPOSITE INDEX: #405 found 41 files doing limit(N) with no orderBy, which returns N ARBITRARY documents; ascending means what falls off the end is the NEWEST claim rather than the oldest and most-forgotten one; and the queue filter and the queue order are the SAME FIELD, so this is a single-field index Firestore maintains automatically and firestore.indexes.json - which is not deployed by deploy-rules.yml and where an index would be INERT while the query threw failed-precondition in production - is untouched. THE COUNT IS EXACT OR IT SAYS IT IS NOT: it reads CEILING + 1 rows, so a result at or under the ceiling is exactly the queue length and a result over it renders as an honest overflow. A second count() aggregation was REJECTED rather than overlooked - two round trips against a queue that changes between them can disagree, producing a badge saying 7 over a list of 6. A FAILED READ IS NOT AN EMPTY INBOX and answers 500 rather than [], because painting 'Nothing to confirm' over a church with people waiting is the Silent-Failure Rule exactly.

THE-351 ADDS this route: one button, and the church - not Harvest - is what it records. IT CALLS THE-350'S WRITER AND WRITES NO INVOICE ITSELF, which that module's own header asked for in advance ('THE-351 is the second caller this exists for, and it calls THIS FUNCTION'); its signature takes an amount, an email, a description and a source rather than a contact for exactly this call, and source: 'event_manual' is what keeps a gift a church vouched for separable from one a processor cleared the day a real rail exists. One press therefore reaches the dashboard figure, accounting, the giving statement, the member's own history and their receipt with NO new reader anywhere. IDEMPOTENCE IS A TWO-PHASE LOCK ON THE REGISTRATION, because the invoice write cannot be inside the transaction - it is a different collection reached through a different module: the transaction returns an existing paymentInvoiceId rather than writing again (the guard that holds forever), refuses a second press while one is in flight (the guard that closes the race), and the lock EXPIRES so a crashed request cannot strand a person unconfirmable. A double invoice is a FALSE FINANCIAL RECORD - the church's books, the dashboard and the member's giving statement would all say they gave twice - so this is asserted by pressing twice rather than described. A FAILED CONFIRMATION WRITES NO PAYMENT STATE AT ALL: the lock is released, paymentInvoiceId stays absent, paymentStateOf still reads 'claimed', the queue key is still there so the row is still in the inbox, and the response carries the failure for the admin to read; there is no path that reports a confirmation without an invoice id behind it. WHO AND WHEN are stamped on the registration and the admin's uid reaches the invoice through THE-350's own recordedBy, because if a member disputes the gift later the church needs the name of the admin who vouched and Harvest has no opinion of its own to offer.

THE-351 ADDS this component: the per-tenant inbox, in every tenant, top right on BOTH shells. components/PlatformInbox.tsx was read and its SHAPE followed - a list, a row, a state the reader changes - while its COLLECTION and its SCOPE were deliberately not reused: platform_inbox has no tenant in its path at all, and one church seeing another's payment claims is the failure this ticket must make impossible. It also does the two things this must not - limit(300) with NO orderBy, which is #405's defect, and a client Firestore listener - so this reads an Admin-SDK route that orders ascending under a ceiling and reports whether its count is exact. THE ROW IS HALF A RECONCILIATION, NOT A NOTIFICATION: the founder said 'the guy who presses the confirmation button checks the church bank first', so it carries WHO, HOW MUCH, WHICH LINE (the reference), WHERE TO LOOK (the provider) and WHEN - drop the reference and the admin is matching on name and amount, which collides the first time two people from one family pay for the same ticket type. THE BADGE READ IS DEFERRED BY ONE MACROTASK AND DEDUPED ACROSS REMOUNTS, which is THE-139's property (the cost of a session does not grow with navigation) and was found by measurement rather than by inspection: read on the mount tick, it starved the entitlement lookup the nav itself depends on. Opening the sheet forces a fresh read, so the list an admin works from is never cached and only the badge can age. A failure is a STATE beside the row (THE-321's saveState shape), never a toast, and the row does not move. Every tappable target carries min-h-11 below sm with Rule 4's 38px above, measured in a real Chromium; the file mints no colour literal because bg-gold IS var(--brand-color). NO RAW PIXEL HEIGHT: every control carries min-h-11 (44px off the spacing scale) below sm and spends CONTROL_DENSITY.action above it, so this ticket mints no height of its own - which is what THE-345's height sweep is for, and what a hand-written sm:min-h-[38px] would have broken.

THE-351 ADDS this module: the browser half of the three routes, in ONE place, because TWO SURFACES CONFIRM AND THERE MUST BE ONE CALL. The inbox is where an admin is PROMPTED; the event's attendee list is where they are already standing when they notice an unconfirmed row - and it is the only surface that reaches a member who registered LOGGED OUT and can therefore never press 'I've paid' themselves, a hole the inbox alone cannot close. A second fetch written inline in the second screen is how two surfaces drift into disagreeing about what a confirmation is. NOTHING HERE CATCHES: a rejection is THROWN for the caller's own saveState machine to render, because a failed confirmation must surface VISIBLY and must not mark the ticket paid, and swallowing it into an { ok: false } a caller might ignore is the silent failure THE-342 named. The badge cache lives here rather than in the component so every mount of the shell shares one answer; it is dropped the moment anything can have moved the queue - a confirmation, whether or not it succeeded, and a member's own press - and a FAILED read is never cached, because caching it would paint an empty inbox over a church with people waiting for the whole TTL.

THE-351 owns this APPEND and removes nothing THE-345 built. Added: MANUAL_EVENT_PAYMENTS_ENABLED (true), ticketPricingAvailable(), manualConfirmationMode() and NOT_CONFIRMED_LABEL. PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED is UNTOUCHED and still false - the naive change, flipping it, would put a price back on the form and send every member into Stripe Checkout against a closed platform account, which is THE-345's own defect one layer along. Two propositions, two lines, exactly the argument THE-345 made when it refused to reuse STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED: one asks whether HARVEST can process a payment, the other whether a CHURCH may collect one itself. Neither implies the other, so the day a rail lands the first can go true while the second stays true for a church that prefers its own Revolut. eventPriceLabel() is BYTE-IDENTICAL and still returns null: THE-345's finding about events/{id}.price is unchanged by manual confirmation - it is quoted on four screens and read by neither the submit route nor PublicEventRegistration, so quoting it would still be a lie - and only ticketTypes[].price, the figure that actually charges, is un-gated. csvAmountCell gains an OPTIONAL third state so its two existing callers and THE-345's own assertions read unchanged; the confirmed branch, and only that branch, divides by 100, because registrations/{id}.amount is CENTS while the older branches render it as dollars - a pre-existing mismatch THE-345 reported rather than changed, unreachable there for any non-zero amount and not acceptable on a cell now carrying a real invoice-backed figure. PAID_EVENTS_HIDDEN_TITLE, PAID_EVENTS_HIDDEN_MESSAGE and NOT_COLLECTED_LABEL are all kept and still reached the day manual confirmation is withdrawn. The file still IMPORTS NOTHING. NO EMOJI: THE-345 wrote this file free of the pictograph range and its own guard sweeps the RAW source for it, so THE-351's additions are written in plain emphasis rather than with the house markers this repo uses everywhere else.

THE-351 owns this change. RE-RECORDED, NOT SUBSTITUTED - THE-326's, THE-345's and THE-346's values stay accepted above. What moved: (1) a DISCLAIMER at the top of the pricing block, above the price input, so an admin cannot type a number without having read that Harvest cannot check anything, that THEY confirm each payment by hand, and that an unconfirmed guest is still let in at the door; (2) a per-event PROVIDER PICKER, checkboxes over the church's own configured giving links, intersected on every read against what the church currently publishes so a deleted link cannot leave a member staring at a dead tile; (3) the ticket-type price input and its clamp move from PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED to ticketPricingAvailable() - the event-level price input is UNTOUCHED and still absent; (4) a payment flag beside each attendee, and a Confirm control on rows that owe money, which exists because a member who registered LOGGED OUT can never press 'I've paid' and would otherwise be unconfirmable; (5) the CSV Amount column consults the row's own state. THE FOUNDER'S DECISION IS STRUCTURAL HERE: the Check In control's condition is byte-identical - r.status === 'confirmed', registration status, which has never meant money - and the flag renders BESIDE it, never in place of it, so no branch in this file can turn a paying guest away. NO FIRESTORE PATH MOVED: the confirm control calls an API route through the shared client module, so firestorePathsOf() is unchanged and this screen still writes only what it always wrote. useTenantOptional() rather than useTenant() is deliberate and not defensiveness: useTenant THROWS outside a provider and a dozen existing suites mount this screen bare. The brand pill spends bg-gold (which IS var(--brand-color)) rather than a sixth var(--brand-color, #d4a017) fallback, so THE-346's colour-literal record for this file is unchanged. THE-308's lazy month-view mount and its own measured suite are byte-identical. NO RAW PIXEL HEIGHT: every control carries min-h-11 (44px off the spacing scale) below sm and spends CONTROL_DENSITY.action above it, so this ticket mints no height of its own - which is what THE-345's height sweep is for, and what a hand-written sm:min-h-[38px] would have broken.

THE-351 owns this APPEND and it is ONE control, rendered twice. The founder: "Put inbox in all tenants in top right where this will appear, that someone pressed on I paid and they have to confirm it." TenantInbox joins the desktop top bar's right cluster - the same cluster the super-admin platform bell has always sat in - and AdminScreenHeader's rightAccessory on mobile, which is the ONLY header a phone renders, so the badge is not shipped to a surface nobody sees. The bottom nav was rejected: it is not 'top right', it is full, and #492 hides it inside a conversation. IT IS NOT THE EXISTING 'inbox' TAB and does not touch it: that tab reads platform_inbox, renders only for a super admin on the apex, and THE-341 already reported that it is labelled 'Platform Inbox' in one nav array and 'Inbox' in another. This ticket adds NEITHER spelling and adds no tab at all; the new control's accessible name is 'Payments to confirm', so no reader, screen reader or test can confuse the two. It renders for every tenant and for nobody on the platform apex, which has no church and therefore nothing to confirm. NO nav array, no group, no permission, no gate, no route, no tab id and no screen mount changed. Its read is deferred by one macrotask and deduped across remounts so THE-139's property - the cost of a session does not grow with navigation - holds, asserted by seven mounts costing at most one read.

THE-351 owns this change and it is the founder's 'registered immediately, marked UNPAID' expressed as a refusal to enter the payment branch. requiresPayment gains && !manualConfirmationMode(), so a priced ticket never reaches a Connect account that does not exist and no member bounces off 'This ministry hasn't set up payments yet' - the exact 400 THE-345 gated the price field to avoid. THE THREE EXISTING BYPASSES ARE UNTOUCHED: amount > 0 && !waitlisted still means a free registration, a waitlist entry and a ticket discounted to zero never reach the question, so a church running a free conference sees nothing this ticket added. The payment fields are spread from ONE object that is {} unless the seat owes money, so a free row cannot gain a field by accident. The reference code is built from crypto.randomBytes through a shared builder and is NOT the ticketCode: that one is what the QR encodes and what opens a door, and this one is written into a payment note - on Venmo, whose transaction feed is PUBLIC BY DEFAULT. The confirmation email gains a payment paragraph for the member who will never see the in-app ticket; it stays INLINE rather than moving to transactional-email.ts because it is one of the nine existing sends THE-340 explicitly left alone, it carries an HTML body with an embedded QR the funnel's text-only signature cannot express, and rewriting a live registration email is not this ticket's risk to take. THE-154's direct charge, the platform fee, the Checkout metadata, the pending-registration rollback, the capacity count, the discount increment, the automated SMS and the CRM activity are all byte-identical, and the suites that pin them now pin manualConfirmationMode() OFF so the rail path keeps proving it is whole for the day it returns.

THE-351 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file. Event gains an optional paymentProviders (typed string[] here so this hook stays free of the provider table; every reader cleans it through readEventProviderIds, which walks the table and drops anything this build does not define). Registration gains the payment fields, and their doc comments carry the rule the rest of the feature rests on: status ABOVE them is REGISTRATION status and has never meant money, and they are separate fields precisely so check-in - which reads status - can never come to depend on whether anybody has paid. NO READ, NO QUERY AND NO FETCH SHAPE MOVED: useEvents' orderBy('startDate','desc').limit(100), useEvent's get and every other hook in the file are byte-identical.

THE-351 owns this change: the member's own ticket now has to say three things about money and not one of them may imply Harvest checked anything. TicketPaymentPanel renders unpaid (the amount, the reference to put in the payment note, the church's chosen links, and 'Harvest does not handle this money and cannot see it'), claimed ('Harvest has not checked anything and cannot... bring it anyway, you will not be turned away at the door') or confirmed ('Grace Chapel marked this ticket paid... Harvest recorded their word for it'). It takes ui/alert for all three in the DEFAULT variant - none is a failure and none is something the member did wrong. THE SENTENCE BESIDE 'I've paid' IS NOT IN A TOOLTIP, and that rejection is the premise of the ticket: a member who believes the press settled it will arrive at the door believing they are paid, and a phone has no hover to reveal the correction with. A failed press renders in place and changes nothing - claimPaymentSent throws rather than resolving quietly. A FREE ticket renders none of this at all. The QR, the ticket code, the waitlist copy and the list itself are untouched; useTenantOptional() is used for the church's name for the reason AdminEvents gives. __TicketPaymentPanel is exported under a dunder name as a TEST SEAM rather than as part of this module's surface, because reaching its four states through the list, the modal and a mocked route would be three fixtures deep before the first assertion. NO RAW PIXEL HEIGHT: every control carries min-h-11 (44px off the spacing scale) below sm and spends CONTROL_DENSITY.action above it, so this ticket mints no height of its own - which is what THE-345's height sweep is for, and what a hand-written sm:min-h-[38px] would have broken.

THE-351 owns this APPEND: the payment instruction on the ONE screen a LOGGED-OUT registrant is guaranteed to see, since the claim route requires a verified identity (a button anyone could press for anyone else's ticket would fill a church's inbox with strangers). It names the church as the party that collects and as the party that decides, and claims nothing about what Harvest checked. ui/alert was deliberately NOT used here: this is the public event shell, which carries none of the admin app's primitives, and importing a second visual vocabulary onto a public surface for one paragraph would be a design change smuggled in behind a data fix. THE STRIPE-RETURN BRANCH IS UNTOUCHED and still reads 'Payment received - you're registered!', which is TRUE there and only there: a rail really did take the money and really did tell Harvest so. That branch is unreachable under manual confirmation, and deleting a true sentence from a dormant path would be this ticket vandalising another feature on its way past - so THE-351's guard is POSITIONAL, allowing the phrase inside that branch and nowhere else in the file. The registration form, the discount lookup, the capacity copy and the registration URL are byte-identical.

THE-351 owns this APPEND. Each ticket now carries its payment STATE - derived SERVER-SIDE by paymentStateOf rather than sent as raw fields, so the client cannot form a second opinion about what 'paid' means and 'confirmed' stays keyed on the invoice id only the confirm route can write - plus its reference code and the church's payment links for that event, re-validated on read through readGivingLinks so a link the church has since broken stops being an href on a member's ticket at the same moment it stops being one on the Give page. ONE tenant-document read serves every row. The dual uid/email match, SHOWABLE_STATUSES, the event join and the 500-row bounds are byte-identical, and a tenant read that fails still returns the ticket - the reference is on the row either way, so the member can still be told what to put in the note.

THE-351 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-350 owned the one before it and THE-349 the one before that. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 67 -> 68 and this ticket's guard suite joins RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-350's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-351 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere: a per-tenant inbox is the shape that usually needs a rule and this one needed none, because a claim and its confirmation are FIELDS on tenants/{t}/registrations/{id} whose read rule already scopes by the PATH, and because the member's write goes through the Admin SDK behind an ownership check stricter than the rule would have been rather than loosening a rule on a document carrying a money amount.

THE-351 owns this APPEND: two adopters join RECORDED_ADOPTERS, each naming its ticket and the primitives it REJECTED per element, which is what that list is for. inbox/TenantInbox.tsx takes sheet (a side surface an admin works down, the shape nav-rail already uses) and rejects dialog (modal and centred - right for a decision, wrong for a queue) and popover (far too small for a row carrying a name, an amount, a reference, a provider and a timestamp); it takes item, empty, and alert TWICE in two variants that are a distinction rather than a style - default for the founder's rule stated to the person about to press the button, destructive for a READ THAT FAILED, which THE-342 reserves red for and which must never be painted as 'Nothing to confirm'; it rejects button for Confirm (a second button vocabulary would make one sheet the only place in the admin app that looks different), sonner (a toast leaves while the money it described is permanent) and table. UserEvents.tsx takes alert for the member's three payment states and rejects tooltip for the sentence beside 'I've paid' - that rejection IS the premise of the ticket, because a member who believes the press settled it arrives at the door believing they are paid and a phone has no hover to reveal the correction with. No entry above was removed or rewritten and no assertion in this suite changed.
